title: DJemma: Hands-Free Music-Making with On-Device Gemma
gist: DJemma is a hackathon app that lets people who cannot use touch or voice (e.g. with cerebral palsy) make music with head and face gestures, with Gemma 4 E2B on LiteRT-LM acting as an on-device DJ, image-to-mix interpreter and word predictor, fully offline on a mid-range Samsung phone. Key lessons: keep the ~1 s/decision model out of the millisecond timing loop, constrain small models to a fixed command vocabulary, and show the AI's actions in plain words; the team (Staxel AI) plans to bring this to touchless accessibility products.

insights.claim: Existing phone head-control features usually emulate a finger with one gesture per tap, which works for menus but not expressive tasks, leaving people who cannot use touch or voice (e.g. with cerebral palsy) underserved.
insights.speaker: Dima Dobrynin
insights.so_what: On-device AI that interprets intent opens an accessibility market that gesture-to-tap emulation cannot serve.
insights.quote: That works for menus, not for anything expressive.

insights.claim: DJemma lets users play melodies by turning their head to pick a note and opening their mouth to play it, with notes snapped to scale and beat so there are no wrong notes, while eye widening adjusts tempo.
insights.speaker: Dima Dobrynin
insights.so_what: Constraining outputs to always-valid results is a key UX pattern for low-precision input modalities.

themes.theme: Fully on-device Gemma on a mid-range phone

insights.claim: DJemma runs MediaPipe Face Landmarker for face tracking and Gemma 4 E2B via LiteRT-LM for everything else, entirely on a mid-range Samsung Galaxy S26 FE without requesting internet permission, demoed in airplane mode.
insights.speaker: Dima Dobrynin
insights.so_what: Small multimodal models now run alongside camera tracking and audio on mid-range phones, widening the addressable device base for on-device AI.

insights.claim: A single Gemma 4 E2B model performs three jobs in DJemma — DJ backing-track control, reading mood photos with vision, and next-word prediction for head-typing — while being small enough to share the phone with camera, tracking and audio.
insights.speaker: Dima Dobrynin
insights.so_what: Multi-role small models reduce on-device memory footprint, a key enabler for consumer edge AI.

insights.claim: DJemma prefilled each system prompt ahead of time so each request processes only its own few lines, a latency optimisation for on-device LLMs.
insights.speaker: Dima Dobrynin
insights.so_what: Prompt-prefix caching is a cheap, broadly applicable edge-latency win.
insights.locator: To keep it fast, we prefilled

themes.theme: Design lessons for small on-device models

insights.claim: Gemma takes about a second per decision while music needs millisecond timing, so DJemma split into a fast camera-to-sound loop and a slow Gemma-to-backing-track loop; devices that perceive, reason and act should assign each part to a loop early.
insights.speaker: Dima Dobrynin
insights.so_what: Separating real-time control from slow LLM reasoning is a general architecture pattern for robotics and interactive edge AI.
insights.quote: Keep the model out of the timing loop.

insights.claim: A small on-device model reliably picks from a short list of well-described commands (intensity, layers, tempo, key, preset) better than producing free text, and capping it at two changes per decision prevented overreaction.
insights.speaker: Dima Dobrynin
insights.so_what: Constrained-vocabulary outputs make small models production-reliable, reducing the need for larger cloud models.
insights.quote: A fixed vocabulary beats free text.

insights.claim: DJemma validates and clamps every model command and drops malformed output so the model cannot break the music.
insights.speaker: Dima Dobrynin
insights.so_what: Deterministic guardrails around LLM output are essential for real-time consumer apps.
insights.locator: The app validates and clamps every command

insights.claim: Merging DJemma's separate Play and Band screens into one screen that writes out the AI's changes in plain words made the concept click instantly for users.
insights.speaker: Dima Dobrynin
insights.so_what: Visible AI actions drive user comprehension and adoption of AI features.

insights.claim: For head-typing, predictions should run in the background with old suggestions kept on screen and a simple offline fallback predictor, and a one-gesture undo matters more than prediction accuracy.
insights.speaker: Dima Dobrynin
insights.so_what: In accessibility UX, recovery from errors beats model accuracy — a product priority signal.
insights.quote: A one-gesture undo matters more than prediction accuracy.

insights.claim: Staxel AI has already added head tracking to Staxel TouchlessOS as an accessibility mode on its public displays, which turn displays into touchless surfaces using a standard webcam and on-device AI.
insights.speaker: Dima Dobrynin
insights.so_what: Hackathon prototypes are moving into commercial touchless-display products.

insights.claim: Staxel plans to upgrade Staxel Board, its iOS-only touchless letterboard for non-verbal people, with head tracking, Gemma 4-powered word and intent prediction and an Android version, and to bring Gemma 4 to adaptive learning games and intent-aware public displays.
insights.speaker: Dima Dobrynin
insights.so_what: Open on-device models are lowering the cost of assistive-tech products — watch for accessibility as an edge-AI growth niche.
